title: a_e (silent e)
parentNote: This is the third vowel to get the silent e, and the one that pays off most, because a_e is everywhere: cake, made, name, plate. The e still says nothing and still reaches back over one consonant to tell the a to say its own name — the ay sound your child spent yesterday listening for. Two things go wrong. The first is reading straight past the e, so cape comes out cap; cover the e with your finger, read the short word, then lift the finger and read it again — cap and cape, tap and tape, plan and plane. The second is the sound itself: ay starts with the mouth open and finishes in a smile, and a child whose jaw never moves says "keck" for cake, so say it slowly and let them watch your mouth close. One warning: have is spelled exactly like these words and ignores the rule completely. If it comes up, just tell them so — it is an old cheat and not something they got wrong.

activities.mouthCue: Your mouth opens wide, then slides up into a smile. Two shapes, one sound: ay.
activities.prompt: The e on the end says nothing. It reaches back over the k and tells the a to say its own name — the sound you hunted yesterday.
Two of these are an a. Which one has the silent e waiting at the end?
All three have a gap and a silent e. Listen to the vowel that goes in the gap.
Three sounds, not four. The k and the e go together and the e stays quiet.
Same start as cake. Only the lump at the end is different.
Two sounds at the front, and the quiet e still at the back.
Same three letters at the front. One of them has the silent e on the end.
Listen to the middle sound. Short a, or the a saying its name?
One you can eat and one you should not. Listen right to the end of it.

activities.text: Meg made a cake, and Tim ate the lot!
A snake came up the lane and hid in the shade.
The plane came in late, and Meg did not wave at it.

activities.title: The snake and the cake
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Meg made a cake and set it on a plate.
They came up the lane and sat in the shade at the lake.
Then a snake came up and did grab the cake!
Meg and Tim did run at it, but the snake did not shift.
It had a big lump in it. The lump is the cake!
They gave the snake a name. It is Cake Snake!
Meg made the same cake at home, and Cake Snake did not get it.
